goal.sl: Poveš, kaj kdo ima (I've got, she's got) in česa nima, vprašaš Have you got …? s kratkimi odgovori, sam have pa rabiš za obroke in kot ameriška angleščina.
goal.de: Du sagst, was jemand hat (I've got, she's got) und nicht hat, fragst Have you got …? mit kurzen Antworten und sagst have allein für Mahlzeiten und wie das amerikanische Englisch.
goal.it: Dici che cosa ha qualcuno (I've got, she's got) e che cosa non ha, chiedi Have you got …? con le risposte brevi e usi have da solo per i pasti e come l'inglese americano.
goal.en: You can say what people have got (I've got, she's got) and haven't got, ask Have you got …? with short answers, and use have alone for meals and as American English does.

say.sl: **have got** pove, kaj imaš: **I've got a dog.** (Imam psa.) Pri **I**, **you**, **we** in **they** je **have got**, kratko **'ve got**: **We've got a cottage.** (Imamo hišico.) **They've got two horses.** (Imajo dva konja.) Britanska angleščina to reče vsak dan.
say.de: **have got** sagt, was dir gehört: **I've got a dog.** (Ich habe einen Hund.) Bei **I**, **you**, **we** und **they** heißt es **have got**, kurz **'ve got**: **We've got a cottage.** (Wir haben ein Häuschen.) **They've got two horses.** (Sie haben zwei Pferde.) Im britischen Englisch sagt man das jeden Tag.
say.it: **have got** dice che cosa è tuo: **I've got a dog.** (Ho un cane.) Con **I**, **you**, **we** e **they** è **have got**, breve **'ve got**: **We've got a cottage.** (Abbiamo una casetta.) **They've got two horses.** (Hanno due cavalli.) L'inglese britannico lo dice ogni giorno.
say.en: **have got** says what is yours: **I've got a dog.** (I have got). With **I**, **you**, **we** and **they** it is **have got**, short **'ve got**: **We've got a cottage.** **They've got two horses.** British English says it every day.

examples.en: We've got a cottage by the beck.
examples.de: Wir haben ein Häuschen am Bach.
examples.it: Abbiamo una casetta vicino al ruscello.

say.sl: Pri **he**, **she**, **it** in enem imenu je **has got**, kratko **'s got**: **Jack's got a sheepdog.** (Jack ima ovčarskega psa.) **She's got a garden.** (Ona ima vrt.) Tu je **'s** **has**, ne **is**: **he's got** = he has got. **It's got a red roof.** (Ima rdečo streho.)
say.de: Bei **he**, **she**, **it** und einem Namen heißt es **has got**, kurz **'s got**: **Jack's got a sheepdog.** (Jack hat einen Hütehund.) **She's got a garden.** (Sie hat einen Garten.) Hier ist **'s** **has**, nicht **is**: **he's got** = he has got. **It's got a red roof.** (Es hat ein rotes Dach.)
say.it: Con **he**, **she**, **it** e un nome è **has got**, breve **'s got**: **Jack's got a sheepdog.** (Jack ha un cane pastore.) **She's got a garden.** (Lei ha un giardino.) Qui **'s** è **has**, non **is**: **he's got** = he has got. **It's got a red roof.** (Ha il tetto rosso.)
say.en: With **he**, **she**, **it** and one name it is **has got**, short **'s got**: **Jack's got a sheepdog.** **She's got a garden.** Here **'s** is **has**, not **is**: **he's got** = he has got. **It's got a red roof.**

say.sl: Za zanikanje gre **not** za have: **I haven't got** (nimam), **he hasn't got** (nima): **I haven't got a car.** (Nimam avta.) **Sam hasn't got a dog.** (Sam nima psa.) **We haven't got time.** (Nimamo časa.)
say.de: Zum Verneinen kommt **not** nach have: **I haven't got** (ich habe kein), **he hasn't got** (er hat kein): **I haven't got a car.** (Ich habe kein Auto.) **Sam hasn't got a dog.** (Sam hat keinen Hund.) **We haven't got time.** (Wir haben keine Zeit.)
say.it: Per dire di no, **not** va dopo have: **I haven't got** (non ho), **he hasn't got** (non ha): **I haven't got a car.** (Non ho la macchina.) **Sam hasn't got a dog.** (Sam non ha un cane.) **We haven't got time.** (Non abbiamo tempo.)
say.en: For no, **not** goes after have: **I haven't got** (have not got), **he hasn't got** (has not got): **I haven't got a car.** **Sam hasn't got a dog.** **We haven't got time.**

examples.en: I haven't got a car, but I've got a bike.

examples.it: Non ho la macchina, ma ho una bici.

say.sl: Za vprašanje gre **have** ali **has** na začetek: **Have you got a pen?** (Imaš pisalo?) **Has she got a car?** (Ima avto?) Kratki odgovor: **Yes, I have.** (Ja, imam.) **No, she hasn't.** (Ne, nima.) Nikoli *Yes, I've got*.
say.de: Für die Frage kommt **have** oder **has** nach vorn: **Have you got a pen?** (Hast du einen Stift?) **Has she got a car?** (Hat sie ein Auto?) Die Kurzantwort: **Yes, I have.** (Ja.) **No, she hasn't.** (Nein.) Nie *Yes, I've got*.
say.it: Per chiedere, **have** o **has** va all'inizio: **Have you got a pen?** (Hai una penna?) **Has she got a car?** (Ha la macchina?) La risposta breve: **Yes, I have.** (Sì.) **No, she hasn't.** (No.) Mai *Yes, I've got*.
say.en: To ask, **have** or **has** goes first: **Have you got a pen?** **Has she got a car?** The short answer: **Yes, I have.** (never *Yes, I've got.*) **No, she hasn't.**

examples.en: Have you got a map? — Yes, I have.
Has Jack got a car? — No, he hasn't.

say.sl: Sam **have** pomeni isto: **I have a dog**, **she has a car**. Ameriška angleščina reče tako in vpraša **Do you have …?** Prav je oboje. Za obroke in dejanja samo **have**: **have breakfast** (zajtrkovati), **have a cup of tea** (spiti skodelico čaja), **have a shower** (stuširati se), nikoli have got.
say.de: **have** allein heißt dasselbe: **I have a dog**, **she has a car**. Das amerikanische Englisch sagt es so und fragt **Do you have …?** Beides ist richtig. Für Mahlzeiten und Handlungen nur **have**: **have breakfast** (frühstücken), **have a cup of tea** (eine Tasse Tee trinken), **have a shower** (duschen), nie have got.
say.it: **have** da solo vuol dire lo stesso: **I have a dog**, **she has a car**. L'inglese americano dice così e chiede **Do you have …?** Sono giusti tutti e due. Per i pasti e le azioni solo **have**: **have breakfast** (fare colazione), **have a cup of tea** (prendere una tazza di tè), **have a shower** (fare la doccia), mai have got.
say.en: **have** alone means the same: **I have a dog**, **she has a car**. American English says it so, and asks **Do you have …?** Both are right. For meals and actions only **have**: **have breakfast**, **have a cup of tea**, **have a shower**, never have got.

examples.de: Haben Sie ein Zimmer für heute Nacht?

examples.en: Let's have a cup of tea!
